Lena (Runtime): Quick thread from today's all-hands Q: can we clarify the batching heuristic changes in the roadmap? folks asked about dynamic token-aware batching vs fixed-window batching.
Sam (CTO): Sure. Short answer: we plan to ship adaptive token-aware batching (alpha) in H2, fixed-window improvements earlier. Adaptive is higher complexity but better tail-latency for mixed-length workloads.
Omar (MLInfra): The adaptive approach groups by expected remaining tokens + priority. It needs per-request token-estimation from the client or a cheap predictor in the gateway.
Mei (Eng): Are we leaning to require client hints? Some customers won't send token estimates.
Lena (Runtime): We want graceful degradation: use client hint if present, else fallback to quick estimator (first-10-tokens model).
Raj (Perf): Lab numbers on mixed chat workload: fixed-window p99=420ms, adaptive p99=250ms, throughput +18% at same GPU util. I'll upload the microbench artifacts to the perf board.
Tessa (SRE): Important: adaptive batching adds variability in slot occupancy. Need new SLO calc for p99 budget. Ops: don't auto-scale based solely on avg token/sec; use 95th token/sec window.
Priya (Product): From PM side, do we expect any change in cost metric customers see? e.g., billed tokens vs latency tradeoffs?
Sam (CTO): Cost per token is unchanged, but effective latency improvements may reduce total tokens for some workloads (fewer retries). We'll include examples in the release notes.
Anil (Customer Success): Can we make adaptive batching opt-in per-tenant initially? Enterprise customers prefer control over scheduling changes.
Lena (Runtime): Yes, per-tenant flag via tenant-config. Default on for hosted trial tenants, opt-in for Dedicated/Private until we validate.
Mei (Eng): How does KV/prefix caching play with batching? We saw cases where large KV size stalls the batch.
Omar (MLInfra): We're adding cache-size-aware batching: if request hits large KV, route to a separate low-latency lane or smaller batch. Also adding async KV prefetch for repeated prefixes.
Raj (Perf): Benchmark: requests with KV>2MB increase p99 by 3x when colocated with short requests. Isolating KV-heavy to a dedicated queue drops regressions to <10%.
Tessa (SRE): We'll need cluster tags to pin low-latency lanes to specific GPU types to avoid noisy neighbors. Ops ticket inbound.
bench-bot: microbench uploaded: artifact://bench/1876500000/adaptive-vs-fixed.tar.gz (contains raw numbers, traces).
Priya (Product): Messaging note: we'll coordinate a short doc that explains per-tenant flags + expected perf gains and the Dedicated behavior. I'll own the doc.
Lena (Runtime): Rollout plan proposal: week 0 deploy alpha on canary (5% traffic), week 2 expand to 25% with telemetry, week 4 full for hosted non-Dedicated. Dedicated/Private opt-in for 8 weeks.
Mei (Eng): Can we get an SDK feature flag too, so customers can force legacy batching for debugging?
Lena (Runtime): Yes, adding `batching.experimental.mode = "adaptive"` to SDK.
Anil (Customer Success): Request: capture regression examples with clear repro steps so CS can triage faster.
Raj (Perf): I'll attach a small repro harness that reproduces KV interference and a short set of prompts that show regression.
Sam (CTO): Action items: Lena create rollout RFC + canary scripts (ticket), Omar add estimator & prefetch plan (ticket), Tessa create SLO scaling rule doc (ticket), Raj publish perf artifacts and repro harness, Priya draft customer-facing note.
Lena (Runtime): I'll post the RFC link here when ready. Please comment on the perf thresholds and the Dedicated opt-in language.
Sam (CTO): Thanks all 44d keep this thread for short updates. If anything blocks the canary, DM me.
